name: Gilla Band
label: Rough Trade
lede: Three school friends who wanted to be the Strokes added a drummer, a Rough Trade deal and a singer with a breakdown to write about. Girl Band became Gilla Band, and Pugnello, their fourth album, picked up five stars from the Guardian.

eras.title: Strokes copyists, then a drummer
eras.text: Dara Kiely drummed, Alan Duggan played guitar and Daniel Fox played bass in a school band they now call a poor Strokes imitation. When Kiely moved to the microphone, Adam Faulkner took the stool and the volume went up.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Line of Best Fit: Gilla Band
years.h: Dara Kiely, Alan Duggan and Daniel Fox start Harrows at 16
years.p: Kiely drums, Duggan plays guitar and Fox plays bass. They now call it a poor imitation of the Strokes, and all that survives is some Myspace and YouTube uploads.
years.xp:
Harrows never got a deal. The recordings that exist were uploaded to YouTube and Myspace, and the members have since described the band as a bad copy of the Strokes.

The Line of Best Fit also reports a short-lived emo band called Surface, with Kiely still on drums. When it folded he moved to the microphone and the band went looking for a drummer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Quietus: Mysterious Handsome Men
years.h: Girl Band forms in Dublin, with Adam Faulkner on drums
years.p: A woman in a bar gives her verdict when Duggan asks what she thinks of the name Girl Band, as Kiely tells it to The Quietus. Kiely has moved from the kit to the mic, and Faulkner takes the stool.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the start to July 2011. Duggan told The Quietus the aim was to be 'just not your average indie band', and to get as far from that as possible.

Kiely's version of the name: Duggan turned to the woman and asked what she thought of Girl Band as a name. She said it was disgusting. Her alternative: The Wombats.

eras.title: Small city, long cover
eras.text: Fox told The Quietus that Dublin is pretty small and bands get to know each other fast. Over three years Girl Band put out singles on a local label, stretched a techno track to eight minutes, and got Geoff Travis to come to the shows.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Quietus: Mysterious Handsome Men
years.h: First single 'In My Head' goes out on Any Other City
years.p: The Dublin label puts out a debut the band recorded themselves.
years.xp:
The band recorded their first single and EP themselves, and told The Quietus they cared most about control: 'It sounds exactly how it's meant to.'

Fox on the local scene, same interview: Dublin's small, so you get to know the other bands quickly.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Quietus: Mysterious Handsome Men
yt: 'Busy at Maths' live, Hard Working Class Heroes 2012
years.h: France 98, an EP cut live and self-produced
years.p: Out October 11 on Any Other City as a 12-inch and a download.
years.xp:
Kiely told The Quietus they did 'like fifty takes' of the vocals for a live-recorded EP. Duggan said the point was control: they could sit down and mix it themselves.

Neither was ideology, they said. The records they liked from other bands were made that way.

years.src: Wikipedia: Why They Hide Their Bodies · Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Quietus: Mysterious Handsome Men
years.h: An eight-minute Blawan cover pulls them out of Dublin
years.p: Girl Band take the techno producer's 'Why They Hide Their Bodies Under My Garage?' and build it into a rock track. UK dates follow in April 2013.
years.xp:
The cover was recorded for the Quarter Inch Collective compilation and got, as the band put it, 'loads of plays and loads of Tweets'. One Quietus commenter liked how Kiely pronounces 'garage'. Wikipedia says the exposure led to UK dates in April 2013.

NPR's Otis Hart, quoted on Wikipedia, noted how rare it is for a rock band to cover techno. He said the band's version builds tension slowly and climaxes halfway through with distorted guitar, where Blawan's original repeats a sample over a constant beat for more than six minutes.

years.src: AOL: Gilla Band · Wikipedia: Gilla Band
years.h: 'Lawman' is the 7-inch people ask about
years.p: AOL later calls it the breakout of a run of limited 7-inches on Any Other City.
years.xp:
Girl Band put out several limited 7-inch singles through Any Other City in 2014. AOL's profile picks 'Lawman' as the breakout among them.

It became a staple of their sets for years, and the band were still playing it at Vicar Street in 2019.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · Wikipedia: Holding Hands with Jamie
years.h: Geoff Travis sees a few Girl Band shows, then signs them to Rough Trade
years.p: The label's founder wants to take what they're doing to a bigger scale. The band keep full creative control and production.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Travis wanted to amplify what they were doing on a bigger scale, and that the band kept complete creative autonomy and production control. That set the pattern: every Girl Band and Gilla Band album since has been self-produced.

eras.title: A breakdown, in track order
eras.text: The debut follows its singer's psychotic episode from start to hospital. A US push followed, then cancelled dates and a break.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gilla Band · The Thin Air
yt: Live at the Old Blue Last, London, Jan 2015
years.h: The Early Years puts the singles on one Rough Trade record
years.p: The Any Other City run and the Blawan cover, on 12-inch, CD and download.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the EP to April 21, 2015. The Line of Best Fit's interviewer places it around 2014, so the exact date is in questions.

years.src: The Quietus: Shakedown The Breakdown · Rolling Stone: Holding Hands · Wikipedia: Gilla Band
years.h: Holding Hands with Jamie goes in at number 11 in Ireland
years.p: Self-produced, engineered by Liam Mulvaney and Jamie Hyland, and mixed live on an analog desk.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone said it sounded 'like it was recorded in a meat locker under a fallout shelter', and called Kiely a 'dryly funny' chronicler of everyday hate. The Guardian called it 'an unbroken series of thumping, crashing songs'.

The video for 'Paul' arrived in August, a few weeks ahead of the record.

q: The whole album is based on this psychotic episode I had two years ago.
years.src: The Quietus: Shakedown The Breakdown
years.h: Holding Hands with Jamie retraces Dara Kiely's breakdown, in order
years.p: His mother's advice, Kiely told The Quietus, when the lyrics wouldn't come. The record follows the psychotic episode he had two years earlier, through to hospital.
years.xp:
The lyrics were finished on the last day of recording. The album runs in chronological order through the episode and ends with 'Witchdoctor', which references a period when Kiely wore a woman's jacket and felt elated. After a couple of months in hospital he found meditation and told The Quietus he was 'the happiest I've been, within reason'.

Anything meant anything, he said, including the sentence 'I can't think of anything to write' if that was all there was.

years.src: The Quietus: Shakedown The Breakdown
years.h: A visa problem costs them a January US run with Savages
years.p: When they do tour, New York rooms fill better than an Irish band had reason to expect.
years.xp:
Per The Quietus, they left one American venue in Washington with beers Dave Grohl had left behind, then drove on to the next show.

New York rooms were 70 to 80 percent full, a result the band did not expect.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Talkies · Hot Press: Choice Music Prize · AOL: Gilla Band
years.h: Cancelled tours, then a year off
years.p: AOL reports tours in 2015 and 2017 were cancelled or cut short over wellness concerns. Wikipedia has the band stopping for about a year.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's account of The Talkies says Kiely's mental health worsened and shows were cancelled, followed by a year-long hiatus in 2017. The band reconvened in February 2018.

Hot Press put it as the band stepping quietly out of the spotlight after a run of cancelled tour dates.

eras.title: A mansion in Laois
eras.text: They came back to a cheap mansion, a key of A and an album that includes a recorded panic attack.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Talkies
years.h: Back together at Ballintubbert House, a mansion in County Laois
years.p: Fox found the house through his engineering contacts and got it cheap. Recording continued at Sonic Studios in Dublin and Grand Street in Brooklyn.
years.xp:
Fox said there were lots of good rooms and that not being in a studio meant they got the house 'for buttons'. Duggan described the aim as an audio representation of the mansion itself.

They recorded everything in the key of A around repeating motifs, with Marvin Gaye and Kendrick Lamar on the stereo. Kiely avoided pronouns in the lyrics: 'I' sounded arrogant to him and 'you' accusatory.

years.h: 'Shoulderblades' ends four years of silence
years.p: The single and its video arrive June 7.

years.cap: Gilla Band at Le Guess Who?, Utrecht, November 2019
years.src: Wikipedia: The Talkies · The Line of Best Fit: Gilla Band · Far Out: Talking The Talkies
years.h: Pitchfork gives The Talkies an 8.0 and NME gives it five stars
years.p: It peaks at 11 in Ireland and 73 in the UK. 'Going Norway' and 'Salmon of Knowledge' come out as singles.
years.xp:
Kiely completed a peer-support course on mental health at DCU around this time. He told The Line of Best Fit that the panic attack captured on 'Prolix' is followed by a mindfulness breathing outro, 'Ereignis'.

The band also recorded 'Aibohphobia' by learning it backwards, recording that, then reversing the tape. The lyrics are palindromic.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Talkies · Hot Press: Choice Music Prize
years.h: Vicar Street shows become a live LP
years.p: Recordings from the sold-out autumn 2019 Dublin dates come out in August. The Talkies is shortlisted for the Choice Music Prize.
years.xp: Hot Press's March 2020 piece on the shortlist says Girl Band's debut 'revolutionised the Irish music scene'.

eras.title: New name, studio record
eras.text: A new name, a record made with lockdown time and a proper studio instead of a rehearsal room, and their first full US tour.

years.big: "We apologise for choosing a misgendered name in the first place"
years.src: Stereogum: Girl Band change their name
years.h: Girl Band becomes Gilla Band, and apologises
years.p: The statement says the old name was picked 'from a place of naivety and ignorance'. 'Gilla' is a given name from old Irish.
years.xp:
Stereogum's report of the statement continues: 'and to anyone who has been hurt or affected by it.'

They said they would no longer perform or release records as Girl Band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Most Normal · The Line of Best Fit: Gilla Band · AOL: Gilla Band
years.h: Most Normal is made in a studio, for once
years.p: Recorded at Sonic Studios and their rehearsal space, produced by Fox, with lap steel and organ in the mix. Number 30 in Ireland.
years.xp:
The Irish Times' Eamon Sweeney called Kiely 'often hilariously funny'. Pitchfork's Laura Snapes described the sound as 'unrelenting' with an 'indignant, surreal mania'.

Fox told The Line of Best Fit lockdown gave them time to be more playful. 'Post Ryan' took about a year to finish.

years.src: The Thin Air: A Band Apart · Wikipedia: Most Normal
years.h: First full US tour, with sold-out dates
years.p: The Thin Air calls the February 2023 run a success, and reports the band were already working on a fourth album.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the first full US tour to the album's release in 2022. The Thin Air places a sold-out American tour in February 2023. Both are in questions.

eras.title: Four years, then Pugnello
eras.text: Three Dublin studios, a drum machine, a death in the family and a diagnosis. Metacritic averages 87 across 11 reviews.

years.src: The Line of Best Fit: Pugnello announcement · DIY: Pugnello review
years.h: 'Giraffe' is the first taste of album four
years.p: The single lands in May 2026 and ends up at track eight of Pugnello.
years.xp: DIY described it as morphing into 'a techno shuffle of grotesque proportions'.

years.src: Rough Trade: Pugnello announcement · Stereogum: Pugnello announcement
years.h: 'Placeholder' announces the album, with a Power Rangers grudge
years.p: Kiely says the song examines his comfort distractions. At six, a Christian summer camp laughed at him for saying he wanted to be a Power Ranger.
years.xp:
Kiely said in the statement that he was 'injecting a lethal dose of nothing' and 'blaring a dangerous amount of Coldplay'. He added he had never forgiven the camp leaders about the Power Rangers.

The video was directed by Cuan Roche.

q: We just make music to impress each other really.
years.src: Metacritic: Pugnello · Rough Trade: Pugnello announcement · DIY: Gilla Band talk · DIY: Pugnello review · Beats Per Minute: Pugnello · The Guardian: Pugnello review
years.h: Four years on from Most Normal, Pugnello
years.p: Pitchfork's review, dated September 24, calls it the band's 'most methodical and charged album to date', per Metacritic. The Guardian gives five stars.
years.xp:
Recorded from 2022 to 2026 at Hellfire, Yellow Door Music Studio and Sonic Studios in Dublin. Produced by the band, recorded and mixed by Fox. The Erica Synths Perkons HD-01 drum machine sits at the centre of it, and DIY reports Neil Young's Trans as an influence on the final track.

DIY and Beats Per Minute say it was written after the death of Kiely's father and around his schizophrenia diagnosis, which he had avoided for years. Metacritic lists 87 across 11 reviews. Beats Per Minute gave it 92 percent. The Guardian's Alexis Petridis called it the work of a band 'audibly and thrillingly out on their own'.
